q: בן 78, ברקע PAF, סוכרת, היפרליפידמיה, ומחלת לב איסכמית. התקבל למחלקת שיקום לאחר שהיה מאושפז במחלקה נוירולוגית עקב שבץ מוחי (CVA). בקבלתו לשיקום, הומלץ על טיפול ב- ATORVASTATIN (LIPITOR) במינון גבוה. הפיזיותרפיסט חושש שהטיפול בסטטינים יפגע בשרירים ויפריע לתהליך השיקומי. מה נכון לגבי מיופתיה על רקע שימוש ב- Lipid lowering agents ?
o: כ- 1% מהמטופלים בסטטינים יכולים לפתח רבדומיוליזיס
רוב המיופתיות מתייצגות תוך חודש מתחילת הטיפול בסטטינים
עליה של CPK נצפית בעד 10% מהמטופלים בסטטינים
טיפול ב- AMIODARONE יכול לעלות סיכון למיופתיה של סטטינים
explanation:
**Amiodarone** is among drugs involved in cytochrome P450 interactions, particularly CYP3A4, that increase the risk of statin-associated myopathy. The stem does not state that this patient takes amiodarone (Hazzard 8e, p. 1598).

**A. Approximately 1% of statin users develop rhabdomyolysis.** Wrong, the source describes rhabdomyolysis in approximately 0.1%; the option assigns this serious complication a higher frequency than the source (p. 1598).
**B. Most myopathies present within one month of starting a statin.** Wrong, median time to symptom onset is six months, and onset may occur after four years. One month is therefore not the window containing most cases (p. 1598).
**C. CPK elevation occurs in up to 10% of statin users.** Wrong, the book distinguishes myalgia with normal CK from myositis with elevated CK, described in approximately 1%; the option's frequency should not be assigned to enzyme elevation (p. 1598).
**D. Amiodarone can increase statin myopathy risk.** Correct, amiodarone is listed among drugs that may interact through statin metabolic pathways and increase myopathy risk, making this relevant to medication review (p. 1598).

Source: Hazzard 8e, p. 1598.

q: בישראל נשקל מינוי אפוטרופוס לבגיר שאינו יכול לדאוג לענייניו. איזו בדיקה נדרשת ביחס לחלופות למינוי?
o: האם בני המשפחה מעדיפים מינוי על פני סיוע
האם אפשר להשיג את המטרה בדרך מגבילה פחות
האם אבחנת דמנציה מתועדת בתיק הרפואי העדכני
האם מוסד האשפוז מעדיף איש קשר לקבלת החלטות
explanation:
**מינוי אפוטרופוס** מחייב בחינת תנאים מהותיים בחוק הישראלי, ולא בחירה בין קטגוריות ראיות אמריקאיות. יש לבחון אם אפשר להגן על האדם בדרך המגבילה פחות את זכויותיו ועצמאותו, לרבות תמיכה בקבלת החלטות (סעיף 33א, עמ׳ 44–45).
"לא ניתן להשיג את המטרה שלשמה נדרש מינוי אפוטרופוס ולשמור על טובתו של האדם בדרך המגבילה פחות את זכויותיו, חירותו ועצמאותו" (עמ׳ 44).

**א. האם בני המשפחה מעדיפים מינוי על פני סיוע.** שגויה, העדפת המשפחה אינה מחליפה את בחינת החלופות והפגיעה בזכויות (עמ׳ 44, 45).
**ב. האם אפשר להשיג את המטרה בדרך מגבילה פחות.** נכונה, החוק מחייב לבדוק אם חלופה פחות מגבילה תשיג את מטרת ההגנה (עמ׳ 44, 45).
**ג. האם אבחנת דמנציה מתועדת בתיק הרפואי העדכני.** שגויה, אבחנה לבדה אינה עונה על השאלה אם יש חלופה שתשמור על טובת האדם (עמ׳ 44, 45).
**ד. האם מוסד האשפוז מעדיף איש קשר לקבלת החלטות.** שגויה, נוחות המוסד אינה הקריטריון; יש לבחון הגנה על האדם תוך צמצום ההגבלה (עמ׳ 44, 45).

מקור: חוק הכשרות המשפטית והאפוטרופסות, סעיף 33א, עמ׳ 44, 45.

q: What role should cardiac risk measures play in the preoperative assessment of an older patient?
o: Estimate risk from age in place of investigating underlying cardiac disease
Combine cardiac risk assessment with an assessment of frailty
Use preserved ejection fraction to reduce the need to assess cardiac disease
Give cardiac information precedence over investigating a history of stroke
explanation:
**Cardiac risk and frailty** provide complementary information: combining these measures improves model discrimination for postoperative outcomes. Preserved ejection fraction does not remove heart-failure risk, and prior stroke also predicts perioperative cardiac events (p. 375).
"When cardiac risk measures such as the Society of Thoracic Surgery and EuroScore II cardiac surgery risk models are added to frailty measures" (p. 375).
"the results are better model discrimination for postoperative outcomes." (p. 375).

**A. Estimate risk from age in place of investigating underlying cardiac disease.** Wrong, the source states that normal aging does not account for most operative risk and directs clinicians to identify underlying illnesses (p. 375).
**B. Combine cardiac risk assessment with an assessment of frailty.** Correct, the source describes improved postoperative outcome discrimination when cardiac risk measures are added to frailty measures (p. 375).
**C. Use preserved ejection fraction to reduce the need to assess cardiac disease.** Wrong, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction still carries higher cardiac-event risk than absence of heart failure, so preserved function does not replace assessment (p. 375).
**D. Give cardiac information precedence over investigating a history of stroke.** Wrong, a history of stroke predicts perioperative major adverse cardiac events and belongs in the assessment (p. 375).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 375.
ref: Hazzard Ch 27 — PERIOPERATIVE CARE: EVALUATION AND MANAGEMENT· Harrison Ch 50 — Unintentional Weight Loss

q:
בת 89, מאושפזת לשיקום לאחר שבר ב RAMUS PUBIS. ברקע מחלת לב איסכמית, יתר לחץ דם והיפרליפידמיה. באשפוז הופעת גרד עורי והוחל טיפול באנטיהיסטמין. כעת מטופלת בתרופות הבאות:   
 TARGIN (OXYCODONE/NALOXONE) 10 mgX2  
 LERCANIDIPINE (VASODIP) 10 mgX2  
 MIRTAZAPINE (MIRO) 15 mgX2  
 OMEPRADEX 20 mgX2  
 BISOPROLOL (CARDILOC) 1.25 mgX1  
 LORATADINE (LORASTINE) 10 mgX1  
 OXAZEPAM (VABEN) 10 mgX1  
 CALCIUM 600 mgX1  
 VITAMIN D 2000 unitsX1  
 המטופלת מתקדמת בתהליך השיקומי ומתהלכת בהשגחה עם הליכון. מתלוננת על בריחת שתן ללא קשר לשיעול או צחוק. בנוסף, זרם השתן חלש מהרגיל, ובלילה מתעוררת כל שעתיים לשירותים. שוללת עצירות. בדיקת שארית על ידי BLADDER SCAN מדגימה שארית של 300 סמ"ק. מהו הצעד הראשון שיש לנקוט בו, כדי לשפר בצורה הטובה ביותר את ההפרעה בנקיטת שתן שמתוארת?
o: הפסקת הטיפול ב- TARGIN וב- LORATADINE
התרוקנויות יזומות לצורך אימון שלפוחית השתן
הוספת טיפול בחוסם אלפא כגון ALFUZOCIN
המשך טיפול שיקומי. כאשר תגיע לניידות עצמאית, ההפרעה תסתדר
explanation:
The official selection is to stop **Targin and loratadine**. A postvoid residual of 300 mL and weak stream suggest retention and warrant evaluation of medication contributions; narcotic analgesics are listed as potential causes. Loratadine should be reviewed as a possible contributor without claiming that its specific mechanism has been established in this patient (Hazzard 8e, p. 703; application to the stem).

**A. Stop Targin and loratadine.** Correct, this is the official answer. Opioids are listed as a cause of retention, so medication review and removal of a contributor fit the residual volume and weak stream. The source does not prove a specific loratadine mechanism in this patient (p. 703).
**B. Scheduled voiding for bladder training.** Wrong, this may assist voiding but does not remove a possible medication-related cause of retention; this is an inference from the behavioral principles and drug list (pp. 703, 711).
**C. Add an alpha blocker such as alfuzosin.** Wrong, relaxing the bladder outlet does not remove an existing drug that impairs emptying. Inference: without a finding of obstruction, the stem does not justify prioritizing this over medication evaluation (pp. 703, 713–714).
**D. Continue rehabilitation; independent mobility will resolve the problem.** Wrong, improved mobility does not treat a possible medication-related cause of the active emptying problem and is insufficient as the first response (p. 703; inference).

Inference note: Scheduled voiding may assist emptying but does not remove a medication contributing to retention; this combines the behavioral-treatment principles with the drug-related causes (pp. 703, 711). An alpha blocker relaxes the outlet but does not address a contribution from existing drugs, and the stem provides no obstructive finding that would justify preferring it over medication review (pp. 703, 713–714). Continued rehabilitation alone overlooks an active problem requiring intervention; better mobility does not eliminate possible drug-related impaired emptying (p. 703).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 703, 711, 713–714.

q: An 88-year-old man presents with new abdominal pain and acute confusion, without a high fever. Which conclusion about possible serious infection is supported by Hazzard?
o: Continue focused evaluation despite the absence of high fever.
Favor a noninfectious explanation because a high fever is absent.
Attribute the confusion to chronic disease before evaluating for infection.
Confirm infection from a positive culture without checking its clinical fit.
explanation:
**Infection in older adults** may present as a decline in function or mentation rather than prominent fever (p. 1669). Lower baseline temperature and a dampened temperature response can delay recognition (p. 1669). The chapter warns that "cultures identify colonization (eg, asymptomatic bacteriuria) rather than true infection" in some settings, so results require clinical interpretation (p. 1669).

**A. Continue focused evaluation despite the absence of high fever.** Correct, atypical presentation and a dampened fever response warrant thoughtful evaluation despite absent high fever (p. 1669).
**B. Favor a noninfectious explanation because a high fever is absent.** Wrong, a dampened temperature response makes absent high fever an unreliable reason to dismiss infection (p. 1669).
**C. Attribute the confusion to chronic disease before evaluating for infection.** Wrong, infection may present as a nonspecific decline in mentation or apparent worsening of comorbidity (p. 1669).
**D. Confirm infection from a positive culture without checking its clinical fit.** Wrong, a positive culture may represent colonization rather than the cause of nonspecific symptoms (p. 1669).

Source: Hazzard, 8th edition, pp. 1669.

q: An 81-year-old man with chronic kidney disease develops hyperkalemia after spironolactone is added to lisinopril. Which property of spironolactone is relevant to this adverse effect?
o: It promotes potassium loss while interfering with aldosterone action
It spares potassium while interfering with aldosterone action
It promotes potassium loss while enhancing aldosterone action
It spares potassium while enhancing aldosterone action
explanation:
**Mineralocorticoid receptor antagonists** interfere with aldosterone and spare potassium. Hazzard describes spironolactone and eplerenone as "potassium-sparing and interfere with the effect of aldosterone" and recommends close monitoring of renal function and serum potassium during initiation and titration (p. 1181).

**A. It promotes potassium loss while interfering with aldosterone action.** Wrong, interference with aldosterone is accompanied by potassium sparing, not promotion of potassium loss (p. 1181).
**B. It spares potassium while interfering with aldosterone action.** Correct, the combination of potassium sparing and interference with aldosterone is the drug property described by the source (p. 1181).
**C. It promotes potassium loss while enhancing aldosterone action.** Wrong, both elements conflict with the source: the drugs spare potassium and interfere with aldosterone (p. 1181).
**D. It spares potassium while enhancing aldosterone action.** Wrong, potassium sparing is correct, but these drugs interfere with rather than enhance aldosterone’s effect (p. 1181).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8th ed., pp. 1181.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: A 77-year-old woman with diabetes, hypertension, and moderate Alzheimer dementia lives with her daughter, who has discovered medication errors. She takes metformin 1000 mg twice daily, glyburide 10 mg twice daily, lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg nightly, donepezil 10 mg daily, and aspirin 81 mg daily. HbA1c is 7.2%, blood pressure is 145/85, and eGFR is 48. Which statement correctly identifies the source-described hypoglycemia concern in her oral diabetes regimen?
o: Metformin is the higher-risk drug because its main effect is to stimulate insulin secretion.
Glyburide is the higher-risk drug because its long half-life increases hypoglycemia risk in older patients.
Metformin and glyburide have similarly low hypoglycemia risk when used as single agents.
Glyburide is the lower-risk drug because its long half-life reduces hypoglycemia risk in older patients.
explanation:
**Glyburide** is not recommended in older patients because its long half-life is associated with increased hypoglycemia risk (p. 1579). In contrast, “Metformin rarely causes hypoglycemia when used alone” (p. 1576). The source therefore supports reviewing glyburide as the hypoglycemia concern; it does not establish a complete individualized replacement regimen from these data.

**A. Metformin is the higher-risk drug because its main effect is to stimulate insulin secretion.** Wrong, Metformin primarily suppresses hepatic glucose production and rarely causes hypoglycemia alone; enhanced insulin secretion is the mechanism described for sulfonylureas (pp. 1576, 1579).
**B. Glyburide is the higher-risk drug because its long half-life increases hypoglycemia risk in older patients.** Correct, This is the source's stated reason glyburide is not recommended in older patients and supports its review in this regimen (p. 1579).
**C. Metformin and glyburide have similarly low hypoglycemia risk when used as single agents.** Wrong, The source identifies hypoglycemia as the main adverse effect of sulfonylureas, while describing it as rare with metformin alone (pp. 1576, 1579).
**D. Glyburide is the lower-risk drug because its long half-life reduces hypoglycemia risk in older patients.** Wrong, The long half-life is associated with increased rather than reduced hypoglycemia risk, so it is a reason for concern rather than reassurance (p. 1579).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 1576, 1579.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: An 85-year-old woman with urinary incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse wants a nonsurgical mechanical option. A trial of a vaginal pessary is being considered. What is its described mode of action?
o: Electrical stimulation of the bladder through a vaginal device
Mechanical support of pelvic tissues through a vaginal device
Suppression of urine production through pressure on the bladder
Dilation of the urethral lumen through a vaginal device
explanation:
A **vaginal pessary** supports the vagina and increases the tightness of pelvic tissues and muscles. This mechanical support is intended to slow prolapse progression; individual fitting is often needed (p. 716).
"a device to slow the progression of prolapse by adding support to the vagina and increasing tightness of the tissues and muscles of the pelvis." (p. 716).
"Often patients need to be individually fitted with the device." (p. 716).

**A. Electrical stimulation of the bladder through a vaginal device.** Wrong, the described pessary acts through tissue support, rather than electrical stimulation (p. 716).
**B. Mechanical support of pelvic tissues through a vaginal device.** Correct, support of the vagina and pelvic tissues is the mechanism described for women with prolapse and incontinence (p. 716).
**C. Suppression of urine production through pressure on the bladder.** Wrong, the mechanism concerns support of prolapsed tissues, not suppression of urine production (p. 716).
**D. Dilation of the urethral lumen through a vaginal device.** Wrong, the described action is supporting and tightening pelvic tissues, not dilating the urethral lumen (p. 716).

Source: Hazzard’s Geriatric Medicine and Gerontology, 8e, pp. 716.

q: A 78-year-old man is admitted from primary care with three days of acute confusion, unsteadiness, and falls. Six weeks earlier he underwent right hip ORIF, complicated by postoperative delirium that resolved. Discharge medications included tramadol 50 mg every six hours as needed and vitamin D 2000 IU daily. Laboratory results are Na 124, K 3.8, creatinine 1.1, and glucose 98. Which assessment of tramadol is supported by the 2023 AGS Beers Criteria?
o: Review tramadol for its SIADH and hyponatremia risks
Continue tramadol as a treatment that counters SIADH-related hyponatremia
Increase tramadol because its sodium-related risk is a rise in sodium
Continue tramadol because sodium monitoring is unrelated to starting this drug
explanation:
**Tramadol** is included in the Beers caution for drugs that "May exacerbate or cause SIADH or hyponatremia" (p. 2068). The same entry recommends close sodium monitoring when starting or changing doses in older adults (p. 2068). It supports evaluating the exposure in this case, without proving that tramadol caused the confusion or low sodium.

**A. Review tramadol for its SIADH and hyponatremia risks.** Correct, this treats tramadol as a possible contributor, consistent with the stated risk rather than claiming proven causation (p. 2068).
**B. Continue tramadol as a treatment that counters SIADH-related hyponatremia.** Wrong, the warning is that tramadol may cause or exacerbate SIADH or hyponatremia, not counter it (p. 2068).
**C. Increase tramadol because its sodium-related risk is a rise in sodium.** Wrong, the stated sodium-related risk is hyponatremia, so a dose increase is not justified by a supposed opposite effect (p. 2068).
**D. Continue tramadol because sodium monitoring is unrelated to starting this drug.** Wrong, the entry specifically links close sodium monitoring to starting or changing dosages (p. 2068).

Source: AGS Beers 2023, pp. 2068.
ref: Hazzard Ch 22 — MEDICATION PRESCRIBING AND DE-PRESCRIBING

q: בן 83 אמור לעבור בעוד חודש ניתוח אלקטיבי של תיקון הרניה מפשעתית מימין. ברקע: מחלת לב איסכמית, אי ספיקת כליות כרונית, יתר לחץ דם וטרום סוכרת. באק"ג שגרתי נמצא RBBB. בבדיקות המעבדה לפני הניתוח- מדד ויחידות החולה ערכים תקינים Na mmol/L 142 135-146 K mmol/L 5.1 3.5-5.3 CREATININE mg/dL 2.2 0.7-1.3 BUN mg/dL 46 5-25 Glucose mg/dL 117 72-100 מה משפיע על הסיבוכים הקרדיאליים הצפויים לאחר הניתוח?
o: נוכחות טרום סוכרת
Mild Mitral regurgitation
קריאטינין >2
פתולוגיה בבדיקת אק"ג
explanation:
**Renal impairment** is an RCRI component: preoperative creatinine above 2 mg/dL. This distinguishes a defined predictor from general findings; it does not make other heart disease irrelevant (Roshanov et al., Introduction, Table 1).

**A. Prediabetes.** Wrong, the RCRI component is diabetes requiring preoperative insulin, not prediabetes (Roshanov et al., Table 1).
**B. Mild mitral regurgitation.** Wrong as the defined predictor here: RCRI includes heart failure, not mild regurgitation itself. Valvular disease still requires individual assessment (Roshanov et al., Table 1; Hazzard p. 375).
**C. Creatinine above 2.** Correct, the patient’s value meets the RCRI renal criterion (Roshanov et al., Table 1).
**D. An ECG abnormality.** Wrong as a general statement: RCRI does not score every ECG change, and RBBB alone is not one of its six components. This does not make all ECG findings clinically irrelevant (Roshanov et al., Table 1).

**Official answer:** Creatinine >2 (IMA final answer key, December 2021, question 36).

Hazzard links renal insufficiency to perioperative volume and acid-base disturbances. The patient has creatinine 2.2 and known renal impairment, but those pages do not present creatinine above 2 as the rule predicting the cardiac complications asked about (Hazzard 8e, pp. 375–376).

Source completion: The external article supplies the creatinine threshold and index components absent from the Hazzard pages cited in the protected note (Roshanov et al., Introduction, Table 1).

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 375–376; Roshanov PS et al. BMJ Open. 2017;7:e013510, Introduction, Table 1. doi:10.1136/bmjopen-2016-013510. https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5223708/.

labTable.span: מדד ויחידות החולה ערכים תקינים Na mmol/L 142 135-146 K mmol/L 5.1 3.5-5.3 CREATININE mg/dL 2.2 0.7-1.3 BUN mg/dL 46 5-25 Glucose mg/dL 117 72-100

explanationReviewNote: The source supports increased perioperative risk with renal insufficiency; reaching creatinine above 2 as the cardiac-complication criterion also requires that specific cardiac-risk rule, which it does not state.

q: איזו מבין התרופות נוגדות דיכאון הבאות עשויה לגרום להפרעת הקצב באק"ג בתמונה מספר 8?
o: Citralopam ( ציפרמיל)
Duloxetine ( סימבלטה)
Bupropion Hydrobromide (וולבוטרין)
Hypericum perforatum ( רמוטיב)
explanation:
The tracing shows polymorphic ventricular tachycardia, consistent in this question with **torsades de pointes**. Citalopram is associated with QT prolongation, and the review distinguishes it from duloxetine and bupropion at the therapeutic doses studied. This does not imply that the other drugs have no cardiac risk (Aronow and Shamliyan, Citalopram, Bupropion, and Duloxetine sections; attached image).

**A. Citalopram (Cipramil).** Correct, the QT-prolongation association is supported by Hazzard and the review and fits the pattern being tested (pp. 929-930; Aronow and Shamliyan).
**B. Duloxetine (Cymbalta).** Wrong, the summarized evidence did not show QT prolongation at the doses studied, although evidence quality is limited. It therefore does not share the same established association here; this is not a guarantee of no risk in every situation (Aronow and Shamliyan, Duloxetine).
**C. Bupropion hydrobromide (Wellbutrin).** Wrong, the review found no association with QT prolongation at the therapeutic doses examined. That conclusion does not cover overdose or unstudied circumstances (Aronow and Shamliyan, Bupropion).
**D. Hypericum perforatum (Remotiv).** Wrong, according to the official key, but it should not be taught as incapable of prolonging QT: a case report describes QT prolongation and ventricular premature complexes after its use. This limited report does not establish the same arrhythmia shown in the image or risk equivalent to citalopram (Özkan et al., Abstract).

Citalopram is associated with QT prolongation. The image is consistent with torsades de pointes, polymorphic ventricular tachycardia in the setting of prolonged QT; the source does not support the wording "especially escitalopram" (Hazzard 8e, pp. 929-930; inherited Harrison 22e locator: p. 1969, Figure 262-1B).

Note: QT prolongation, ventricular premature complexes, and torsades de pointes are different outcomes, and evidence levels differ between drugs.

Source: Hazzard 8e, pp. 929-930; Aronow WS, Shamliyan TA. Effects of antidepressants on QT interval in people with mental disorders. Arch Med Sci. 2020;16:727-741. doi:10.5114/aoms.2019.86928, drug-specific sections; Özkan H et al. A Rare Cardiac Side Effect of a Herbal Medicine; QT Prolongation Due to Hypericum Perforatum: Case Report. Turkiye Klinikleri J Case Rep. 2014;22:139-141, Abstract; https://www.turkiyeklinikleri.com/article/en-a-rare-cardiac-side-effect-of-a-herbal-medicine-qt-prolongation-due-to-hypericum-perforatum-case-report-69051.html.

explanationSource.note: Checked v74 explanation sentences use Hazzard 8e; the printed IMA 7e reference is retained.

q: בת 72, עצמאית בתפקודה וללא חסר קוגניטיבי פנתה למרפאה עקב כאבי עצמות משניים לגרורות מקרצינומה של הריאה. היא טופלה בבית ב- PARACETAMOL ו- DIPYRONE (.אופטלגין) ללא הטבה. הוחלט על התחלת טיפול באופיואידים. מה יש להדריך אותה עם התחלת הטיפול?
o: הטיפול גורם לעצירות אך יש סבילות (tolerance) שמתפתחת אחרי מספר ימים
הטיפול גורם לבחילות אך יש סבילות (tolerance) שמתפתחת אחרי מספר ימים
יש להימנע מנהיגה כל התקופה בה מטופלת באופיואידים
אם מגיעים למינון מקסימלי של תרופה אופיואידית יהיה צורך לעבור לתכשיר אחר
explanation:
When starting an opioid, distinguish **nausea that may diminish with adaptation** from persistent constipation. Central nervous system adaptation can reduce nausea over the following days, whereas the colon does not adapt in the same way; constipation should not be promised to resolve (Barnes et al., constipation and nausea sections).

**A. Constipation occurs, but tolerance develops within days.** Wrong, tolerance to opioid-induced constipation does not develop as stated; prevention, monitoring and reassessment are needed (Barnes et al., constipation section).
**B. Nausea occurs, but tolerance develops within days.** Correct, the initial emetogenic effects often diminish in the days after starting treatment. Persistent nausea still requires assessment and treatment; a fixed resolution time cannot be guaranteed (Barnes et al., nausea section).
**C. Avoid driving throughout the entire course of opioid treatment.** Wrong, avoid driving during initiation or dose increases until assessment on a stable dose without cognitive impairment. This is neither automatic driving clearance nor a blanket clinical prohibition throughout treatment (PCNOW Fast Fact 248, Driving Safety).
**D. Reaching an opioid's maximum dose requires switching drugs.** Wrong, morphine has no fixed analgesic ceiling dose. Titrate according to effect and toxicity; consider switching for pain control and tolerability rather than an arbitrary ceiling (Quigley, Dose titration and Switching opioids).

Source: Barnes et al. Clin Med. 2025;25:100330, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.clinme.2025.100330; PCNOW Fast Fact 248, Driving Safety, https://www.mypcnow.org/fast-fact/counseling-patients-on-side-effects-and-driving-when-starting-opioids/; Quigley. BMJ. 2005;331:825-829, https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.331.7520.825.

q: בן 91, סובל מממאירות ריאה עם גרורות לעצמות, לכבד ולמוח האונקולוגים החליטו. להפסיק טיפולים כימותרפיים והמליצו על טיפול פליאטיבי בלבד החולה מאושפז כרגע. במחלקה פנימית בשל דלקת בדרכי השתן מי מוסמך להיות "הרופא האחראי" ולהגדיר את החולה כנוטה למות?
o: הרופא האונקולוג המומחה המטפל
כל רופא אונקולוג מומחה
מנהל המחלקה הפנימית
כל רופא מומחה במחלקה הפנימית
explanation:
## הסבר קליני

לפי **חוק החולה הנוטה למות**, הרופא האחראי במוסד הוא מנהל מחלקה או יחידה האחראי לטיפול, או רופא מומחה שמונה לכך בידי מנהל המוסד, המחלקה או היחידה (סעיף 3, עמ׳ 4).

**א. הרופא האונקולוג המומחה המטפל.** שגויה, עצם הטיפול האונקולוגי אינו המינוי המוגדר בחוק. לא נאמר שהאונקולוג הוא מנהל המחלקה האחראית לאשפוז או מומחה שמונה לתפקיד (סעיף 3, עמ׳ 4).
**ב. כל רופא אונקולוג מומחה.** שגויה, התמחות באונקולוגיה לבדה אינה מספיקה; נדרש התפקיד הניהולי האחראי לטיפול או מינוי ייעודי (סעיף 3, עמ׳ 4).
**ג. מנהל המחלקה הפנימית.** נכונה, בהקשר האשפוז המתואר, מנהל המחלקה האחראית לטיפול מתאים להגדרת הרופא האחראי. זו אינה טענה שמומחה אחר לא יוכל להתמנות לתפקיד (סעיף 3, עמ׳ 4).
**ד. כל רופא מומחה במחלקה הפנימית.** שגויה, החוק מאפשר למומחה להיות רופא אחראי אם מונה לכך. האפשרות אינה כוללת את תנאי המינוי ולכן מרחיבה את הסמכות לכל מומחה במחלקה (סעיף 3, עמ׳ 4).

מקור: חוק החולה הנוטה למות, סעיף 3, עמ׳ 4.
